examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{医者|いしゃ}だった。
{祖父|そふ}から{昔|むかし}の{話|はなし}を{聞|き}いた。
examples.english: I heard stories about the old days from my grandfather.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{元気|げんき}です。
{夏休|なつやす}みに{祖父|そふ}の{家|いえ}に{遊|あそ}びに{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to visit my grandfather's house during summer vacation.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{今年|ことし}{八十|はちじゅう}{歳|さい}になるけれど、まだとても{元気|げんき}で{毎日|まいにち}{散歩|さんぽ}している。
examples.english: My grandfather will turn 80 this year, but he's still very healthy and takes a walk every day.

notes:
{祖父|そふ} is the formal term for one's own grandfather, used in polite or written contexts.

FORMALITY LEVELS:
- {祖父|そふ}: formal (own grandfather)
- おじいちゃん: casual/affectionate
- おじいさん: neutral/someone else's grandfather

DISTINGUISHING GRANDFATHERS:
- {父方|ちちかた}の{祖父|そふ}: paternal grandfather
- {母方|ははかた}の{祖父|そふ}: maternal grandfather

RELATED FAMILY TERMS:
- {祖母|そぼ}: grandmother (formal)
- {祖父母|そふぼ}: grandparents
- {曽祖父|そうそふ}: great-grandfather

USAGE NOTE:
Use {祖父|そふ} when speaking about your grandfather to others in formal situations. Use おじいちゃん when speaking directly to him or in casual contexts.
